robot.name: Unitree H1
robot.generation: Unitree's first full-size humanoid; later H1-2 variant
robot.status_notes: Teased 2023-08-15 with an expected price below $90,000. Bought through Unitree sales or distributors rather than a public checkout: Unitree's store shows a $90,000 'Contact us for the real price' listing and a European distributor lists the H1/H1-2 from EUR 93,496 excluding VAT, delivery on request. RoboZaps reports the H1-2 has been delisted from Unitree's own store and that the H1 listing is marked unavailable for direct online purchase, while Unitree's newer H2 ($29,900) is the platform it now promotes. No credible announcement of discontinuation was found.
intended_use_cases: academic research on bipedal locomotion and control
humanoid AI, reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning research

height.notes: Unitree's spec page gives 'about 180CM'; the dimension row lists (1520+285)mm, i.e. 1805 mm. The Robot Report gave 1805 x 570 x 220 mm at launch. The H1-2 variant is 'about 178CM'.

weight.notes: Stock H1 is about 47 kg; the H1-2 variant is about 70 kg. RoboZaps notes that Stanford's research H1, fitted with added wrists, hands and head cameras, weighed 60 kg, so the stock figure understates configured weight.

payload.notes: Unitree publishes no payload figure for the H1 on its product page; 30 kg appears only in the RoboHub directory, which states it does not test robots. The European distributor lists payload as '-' for the H1 and 7-21 kg (rated/peak arm load) for the H1-2. Treat 30 kg as unverified directory data, not a Unitree spec.

runtime.notes: Reported by ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics, added 2026-10-30 by automated spec fill; RoboHub's lineup table lists 2 h; official page gives battery capacity only..

battery.notes: 15 Ah pack at a maximum of 67.2 V, described by Unitree as quickly replaceable. The H1-2 uses the same pack per the developer documentation.

degrees_of_freedom.original_value: 5 DoF per leg + 4 DoF per arm
degrees_of_freedom.notes: Unitree's per-limb counts total 18 (hip x3 + knee + ankle per leg; 4 per arm, expandable). Unitree's own H1 URDF defines 19 actuated joints including a torso joint; RoboHub and RobotsGuide list 19. The H1-2 has 27 DoF. The discrepancy is unresolved.

walking_speed.notes: Unitree claims 3.3 m/s as a world record and 'potential mobility > 5 m/s'. Launch coverage listed 1500 mm/sec and the distributor's description says 'up to 5.4 km/h' (1.5 m/s) while repeating 3.3 m/s in its spec table; RobotsGuide lists 6 km/h. No independently timed speed was found; RoboZaps reports a 10.1 m/s peak from a modified ~62 kg H1 in April 2026 with Unitree conceding a measurement error is possible.

hands.description: The H1 ships without hands: launch images showed only a cushioned nub at the end of each 4-DoF arm, and Unitree lists a dexterous hand as 'Optional'. The H1-2 supports optional Dex5-1 or other ambidextrous hands. Research users added wrists, hands and head cameras themselves.

items: 3D LiDAR + depth camera per Unitree's spec sheet, described as 360-degree depth perception
H1-2 developer documentation identifies the head LiDAR as a Livox MID-360 and the head depth camera as an Intel RealSense D435
no wrist or fingertip force/tactile sensing disclosed for the standard configuration

compute.description: Standard configuration: Intel Core i5 for platform functions and Intel Core i7 for user development, with optional Intel i7 or Nvidia Jetson Orin NX modules (up to three on the H1-2). H1-2 documentation lists a dedicated i5-1235U motion-control computer plus an i7-1255U/1265U development computer with 8-32 GB LPDDR5 and 500 GB+ storage. RobotsGuide lists an Intel i7 main computer with a custom ARM-based controller on each joint and Ubuntu Linux.

actuators.description: Unitree M107 joint motor: peak torque about 360 N.m, peak torque density about 189 N.m/kg, hollow shaft, dual encoders, low-inertia high-speed internal-rotor PMSM, industrial crossed roller bearings. Maximum joint torques quoted for the H1 as knee ~360 N.m, hip ~220 N.m, ankle ~59 N.m, arm ~75 N.m.

availability.notes: No public checkout price. Unitree's store shows a $90,000 'Contact us for the real price' anchor; the European distributor Génération Robots lists the H1/H1-2 from EUR 112,195.20 including VAT (EUR 93,496.00 excluding VAT) with delivery times on request; launch coverage in 2023 said the expected price was below $90,000; RobotsGuide cites US $90,000-110,000. RoboZaps reports the H1-2 has been delisted from Unitree's store and that newer buyers are quoted the $29,900 H2 instead.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Weak. The stock H1 has 4-DoF arms and no hands (a cushioned nub at launch, hands optional). The H1-2 variant adds 7-DoF arms with about 7 kg rated / 21 kg peak arm load and optional Dex5-1 hands. Manipulation results come from labs that rebuilt the robot (Stanford HumanPlus for clothes folding and typing, CMU H2O for teleoperation), reported only through a secondary blog.
caveats: No Unitree-published manipulation demo, success rate or task benchmark for the stock H1.
The HumanPlus/H2O work used modified robots (added wrists, hands, cameras; about 60 kg, 33 DoF) and the papers themselves were not reviewed.
Arena cannot credit dexterity that requires third-party hardware additions.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Unitree states the H1 can walk and run autonomously in complex terrains, and RoboZaps describes a 100 m sprint video as an H1 'running autonomously on a track'. The SDK documentation covers SLAM, high-level motion services, teleoperation and reinforcement-learning routines. No autonomous manipulation, pick-and-place or productive task has been publicly demonstrated.
caveats: Autonomy is claimed for locomotion only, and execution mode in the sprint video is a company statement.
No intervention counts, task completion rates or independent audit.
Teleoperation is a documented use of the platform (CMU H2O, Unitree's own teleoperation docs), so demonstrated motion cannot be assumed autonomous.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Strongest dimension. Unitree claims 3.3 m/s (world record) with >5 m/s potential and 360 N.m knee torque; the H1 won 1500 m (6:34.40) and 400 m (1:28.03) golds at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games, and RobotsGuide credits it with golds in four high-speed disciplines. RoboZaps reports a 10.1 m/s peak from a modified ~62 kg H1 in April 2026. Sixteen H1s performed a choreographed dance on national television.
caveats: The 3.3 m/s 'world record' is company-claimed and video-based, not Guinness-certified; RoboZaps notes the certified bipedal 100 m record still belongs to Cassie.
The 10.1 m/s figure is a peak from a modified robot with no disclosed total time and Unitree's own measurement-error caveat.
No fall-rate, disturbance-recovery or independently instrumented locomotion metric found.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Head-mounted 3D LiDAR plus depth camera for 360-degree depth perception, with SLAM services and SLAM examples in the SDK. H1-2 documentation identifies a Livox MID-360 and an Intel RealSense D435 and publishes the sensor IP addresses. No perception benchmark or task-level perception accuracy is published.
caveats: Sensor models are documented for the H1-2, not explicitly for the stock H1.
No third-party perception evaluation, and the choreography account of robots adjusting to unscripted stage events is second-hand.

human_interaction.summary: The distributor states the H1 has voice and facial recognition for natural interaction; Unitree's developer documentation and app support remote control via app, PC and controller. No conversational or interaction demo, latency data or reliability metric was found.
caveats: Voice/facial recognition is a reseller description, not a Unitree disclosure or a demonstration.
No safety-rated human-proximity behaviour published.

endurance_reliability.summary: Unitree publishes an 864 Wh quickly replaceable battery but no runtime, duty cycle or failure data. Third-party directories conflict (1 hour per RobotsGuide, 2 hours per RoboHub). No field reliability, MTBF or continuous-operation record was found for the H1.
caveats: Runtime is unresolved between sources and unmeasured.
No public intervention, failure-rate or uptime logs; competition outings are minutes-scale.

human_environment_fit.summary: Human-sized biped (about 180 cm, 47 kg, carbon-fibre/aluminium structure) with human-plausible dimensions; the distributor explicitly calls it a prototype for research and development that is not compatible or certified for industrial tasks. Unitree warns users not to modify it dangerously or use it in hazardous ways.
caveats: No safety certification, force-limiting disclosure or human-proximity testing found.
Unitree's product page carries explicit warnings about hazardous use and asks buyers to understand humanoid limitations.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Real but research-and-stage shaped. H1s are used by university labs (Stanford HumanPlus, CMU H2O) and appeared in a televised national performance with 16 units; the robot is purchasable by quote through Unitree and distributors. No named commercial customer, production task, operating hours or output metric was found.
caveats: Research use is reported via a secondary blog citing papers that were not reviewed directly.
The Gala appearance is a choreographed performance, not productive deployment.
No disclosed paid commercial deployment with metrics.

accessibility_value.summary: Priced in the enterprise/research band: a $90,000 contact-us anchor on Unitree's store, EUR 93,496 excluding VAT from a European distributor, and US $90,000-110,000 cited by RobotsGuide. It is not a consumer purchase and Unitree's cheaper successors (G1 $13,500, R1 $4,900, H2 $29,900 per RoboHub) undercut it.
caveats: No published final price; quotes vary with compute, hands and support.
Delisted H1-2 and H2-first marketing suggest limited remaining buyer value for new purchases.

evidence_items.title: Unitree H1 official specification page
evidence_items.claim: Unitree lists the H1 at about 180 cm, about 47 kg, moving speed 3.3 m/s (world record) with potential mobility >5 m/s, 18 DoF by per-limb counts (5 per leg, 4 per arm), 864 Wh replaceable battery, 360 N.m maximum joint torque, 189 N.m/kg peak torque density, 3D LiDAR + depth camera, and optional dexterous hands. The same page lists the H1-2 variant at about 178 cm, about 70 kg and <2 m/s.
evidence_items.notes: Official product page; all numbers are company-published and not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, mass, DoF, speed and battery for cross-robot comparison.
evidence_items.source_location: Unitree H1 product page, 'Unitree H1' specification bullets under Mobility
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company spec page. The 3.3 m/s claim is labelled a world record by Unitree but is not certified; launch coverage listed a slower 1500 mm/sec figure.

evidence_items.title: Unitree's autonomy and terrain claim for H1
evidence_items.claim: Unitree says the H1 can walk and run autonomously in complex terrains and environments, describing it as the first full-size general-purpose humanoid robot that can run in China.
evidence_items.notes: Marketing claim with no task list, intervention count or success rate.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: The only autonomy statement Unitree makes for the H1; it covers locomotion, not manipulation or task completion.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Possessing a stable gait and highly flexible movement capabilities, it is able to walk and run autonomously in complex terrains and environments.
evidence_items.source_location: Unitree H1 product page, 'The first full-size general-purpose humanoid robot that can run in China' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Vendor copy; no execution-mode disclosure, no test protocol, no independent verification.

evidence_items.title: Launch coverage of the H1 teaser
evidence_items.claim: At the 2023-08-15 announcement the H1 measured 1805 x 570 x 220 mm and weighed 47 kg, with 5 DoF legs and 4 DoF arms; launch images showed no hands, only a cushioned nub at the end of each arm, with hands in development. Unitree said the price was expected to be below $90,000, no release date was announced, and the video claimed commercial availability within 3-10 years.
evidence_items.notes: Trade-press reporting of Unitree's own teaser video and X post.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Establishes announcement date, launch configuration and price expectation; also confirms hands were absent at reveal.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: According to Unitree, the price of the H1 is expected to be below $90,000.
evidence_items.source_location: The Robot Report article body, price paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: Reputable trade outlet relaying Unitree's video and post; the embedded video was not reviewed directly.

evidence_items.title: Unitree H1/H1-2 developer documentation
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's official documentation discloses the H1-2 architecture in detail: 27 DoF (7 per arm, 6 per leg, 1 waist), individual joint limits, a Livox MID-360 head LiDAR and Intel RealSense D435 head depth camera, an i5-1235U motion-control computer plus an i7-1255U/1265U development computer, the 864 Wh battery, the M107 motor at 360 N.m with dual encoders, optional Nvidia Orin NX modules, optional Dex5-1 hands, arm rated load about 7 kg and peak about 21 kg, and a moving speed below 2 m/s. The SDK also documents teleoperation, SLAM and reinforcement-learning control routines.
evidence_items.notes: Genuine technical disclosure, but it describes the H1-2, not the stock H1; do not transfer these numbers to the H1.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows the platform's engineering depth and the control/perception interfaces available to labs.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Each arm of the H1-2 possesses 7 degrees of freedom, each leg has 6, and the waist features 1 degree of freedom, culminating in a total of 27 degrees of freedom across the entire machine.
evidence_items.source_location: Unitree documentation centre, H1 SDK Development Guide > About_H1-2, Component Name section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official documentation page (marked last updated 2026-03-12). H1-2-specific; the stock H1 page does not publish comparable joint-level detail.

evidence_items.title: Speed and competition record timeline
evidence_items.claim: RoboZaps dates the 3.3 m/s claim to March 2024 as company-claimed and video-based, records 1500 m gold in 6:34.40 (a Unitree-claimed robot world record) and 400 m gold in 1:28.03 at the first World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing in August 2025, run by a Unitree subsidiary team, and records a 2026-04-14 sprint video with a 10.1 m/s peak from a modified ~62 kg H1 with no total time disclosed and Unitree conceding a measurement error is possible.
evidence_items.notes: Independent desk-research blog; competition results are corroborated by RobotsGuide, sprint details are not.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: The clearest dated mobility evidence for the H1, and an explicit statement that nothing is Guinness-certified.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: At the first World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, the H1 takes 1500 m gold in 6:34.40 (a Unitree-claimed robot world record) and 400 m gold in 1:28.03, run by a Unitree subsidiary team
evidence_items.source_location: RoboZaps H1 review, 'The speed record, dated: from 3.3 m/s to a contested crown' table
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary summary of the linked heise, The Robot Report and SCMP coverage; those articles were not opened in this review. Race times are public-event results, not lab measurements.

evidence_items.title: Price and ordering situation
evidence_items.claim: The H1 is quote-based and enterprise-only: Unitree's store lists 'Unitree H1（Contact us for the real price）' at $90,000 with a contact-sales flow and marks the listing unavailable for direct online purchase; the H1-2 is delisted from the official store and sold out at a distributor; the company's newer H2 lists at $29,900.
evidence_items.notes: Desk research describing the official store; the store page itself was not opened in this review.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Explains why no consumer purchase path exists and why the $90,000 figure is an anchor, not a checkout price.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The official store lists "Unitree H1（Contact us for the real price）" at $90,000, with a contact-sales flow, no spec sheet attached, and the shop's own product data marking the listing unavailable for direct online purchase.
evidence_items.source_location: RoboZaps H1 review, 'The price and ordering situation, in full'
evidence_items.verification_notes: One outlet's reading of shop.unitree.com as of July 2026; not independently re-fetched here.

evidence_items.title: Research adoption of the H1 platform
evidence_items.claim: The H1 is the platform under Stanford's HumanPlus (full-stack imitation learning including folding clothes and typing, June 2024) and CMU's H2O real-time whole-body teleoperation (March 2024), and is a default model in reinforcement-learning and simulation benchmarks. Stanford's configured robot weighed 60 kg with 33 DoF after adding wrists, hands and head cameras.
evidence_items.notes: Named academic users described by a secondary blog that cites the arXiv papers; the papers were not reviewed directly.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Best evidence of a real installed base, but the work reflects lab-added hardware and lab-written software, not the shipped product.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: the platform under research that shaped the field, from Stanford's HumanPlus to CMU's H2O
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary reporting; no customer or institution statement was reviewed. Configured weight and DoF differ from the stock robot.

evidence_items.title: DoF discrepancy: 18 versus 19
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's spec page publishes per-limb counts totalling 18 (5 per leg, 4 per arm, no torso row) while Unitree's official H1 URDF defines 19 actuated joints including a torso joint; both are manufacturer-sourced, so the total DoF is unresolved.
evidence_items.notes: Documented conflict rather than a settled figure; specs record 18 with the conflict noted.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Affects DoF comparisons between humanoids; a one-joint difference is minor for scoring.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Both are manufacturer-sourced, from different layers: the unitree.com spec page publishes per-limb counts totaling 18 (5 per leg, 4 per arm, no torso row), while Unitree's official H1 URDF engineering file defines 19 actuated joints, including a torso joint
evidence_items.source_location: RoboZaps H1 review, 'The misinformation audit' table, 19 DoF vs 18 DoF row
evidence_items.verification_notes: The URDF itself was not inspected in this review.

evidence_items.title: RoboHub directory entry for the H1
evidence_items.claim: RoboHub's lineup table lists the Unitree H1 at 30 kg payload, 3.3 m/s, 2 hours runtime, 19 DoF, 47 kg, price state 'Request quote', while stating that values come from manufacturer pages and that RoboHub does not test robots.
evidence_items.notes: Aggregator data; the 30 kg payload and 2 h runtime do not appear on Unitree's H1 page and conflict with other directories.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Explains where the widely quoted 30 kg payload and 2 h runtime originate; low trust.
evidence_items.source_location: RoboHub Unitree brand page, 'Lineup specifications' table, H1 row
evidence_items.verification_notes: Directory aggregation with no primary citation for payload or runtime; explicitly untested.

evidence_items.title: RobotsGuide spec sheet and runtime conflict
evidence_items.claim: RobotsGuide lists the H1 at 180 cm, 57 cm length, 22 cm width, 47 kg, 6 km/h standard speed, 19 DoF, 19 brushless DC motors, carbon fibre and aluminium construction, an Intel i7 main computer with a custom ARM controller per joint, Ubuntu Linux, an 864 Wh lithium-ion pack with '1 hour of operation', and a cost of US $90,000-110,000.
evidence_items.notes: Encyclopedia entry that conflicts with Unitree and with RoboHub on DoF, speed and runtime.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supplies the only 1-hour runtime figure, which conflicts with the 2-hour directory figure; neither is measured.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 864 Wh lithium-ion battery pack, 1 hour of operation
evidence_items.source_location: RobotsGuide Unitree H1 page, Specs > Power
evidence_items.verification_notes: Directory content with no stated test method; not a measurement.

evidence_items.title: World Humanoid Robot Games results (second source)
evidence_items.claim: RobotsGuide credits the H1 with gold medals in four high-speed disciplines at China's inaugural World Humanoid Robot Games, corroborating the 1500 m and 400 m wins reported by RoboZaps.
evidence_items.notes: Directory claim corroborating a competition result reported elsewhere; no event results table was reviewed.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Second, independent-of-Unitree source for the H1's public race record.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: H1 dominated the track events at China's inaugural World Humanoid Robot Games, earning gold medals in four high-speed disciplines.
evidence_items.source_location: RobotsGuide Unitree H1 page, 'Did you know?' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Encyclopedia summary; individual event times and conditions not published here.

evidence_items.title: Reseller listing, price and positioning
evidence_items.claim: Génération Robots lists the H1/H1-2 from EUR 112,195.20 including VAT (EUR 93,496.00 excluding VAT) with delivery on request, publishes H1 18 DoF / 47 kg / 3.3 m/s and H1-2 27 DoF / 70 kg / <2 m/s / 7-21 kg arm load with the H1 payload row left blank, and states that the humanoid is a prototype for research and development, not compatible or certified for industrial tasks. It also claims voice and facial recognition.
evidence_items.notes: Distributor with an actual listed price; its positioning statement is unusually candid about readiness.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Gives a real transaction price band and a vendor-side statement that the robot is not certified for industrial work.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: This humanoid robot is a prototype for research and development, not compatible or certified for current or industrial tasks.
evidence_items.source_location: Génération Robots H1/H1-2 product page, description header
evidence_items.verification_notes: Reseller marketing plus a readiness disclaimer; prices are list prices 'from', not quotes for a specific configuration.

evidence_items.title: Sixteen H1s at the 2025 Spring Festival Gala
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's own site records that 16 H1 robots, directed by Zhang Yimou, performed the dance piece 《秧Bot》 on CCTV's Spring Festival Gala in 2025.
evidence_items.notes: Company statement about a nationally televised event; the performance itself is publicly observable.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Largest known simultaneous H1 deployment (16 units) and evidence of multi-robot choreography and stage robustness.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: 2025年2月28日，由张艺谋导演，16台Unitree H1表演的《秧Bot》惊艳亮相中央广播电视总台蛇年春节联欢晚会。
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official page; the broadcast was public but this review did not watch it. RoboZaps adds that the robots spun and threw/caught handkerchiefs and used LiDAR to adjust to unscripted events, which is second-hand.

evidence_items.title: H1 versus H1-2 specification separation
evidence_items.claim: Unitree states that the H1-2 is an upgrade of the H1 with more motion capability and degrees of freedom, and publishes different figures for each (H1: 47 kg, 18 DoF, 3.3 m/s; H1-2: 70 kg, 27 DoF, <2 m/s, 7 kg rated / 21 kg peak arm load).
evidence_items.notes: Guards against the common conflation of H1 and H1-2 numbers in third-party summaries.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents mis-crediting H1-2 manipulation capability to the H1.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: H1-2 has been upgraded based on the H1 model, boasting enhanced motion capability and degrees of freedom.
evidence_items.source_location: Unitree documentation centre, About_H1-2, Component Name section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official documentation plus the official product page parameter table.

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures for the H1
evidence_items.claim: No Unitree-published payload, runtime, hand DoF, failure rate, intervention count, task success rate, commercial deployment metric, safety certification or independent benchmark was found for the H1; the videos reviewed for this pack had no transcripts and were not used to characterise demonstrated behaviour.
evidence_items.notes: Gap list from this review, not evidence of inability.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should keep confidence low on payload, endurance, autonomy and commercial proof.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure. Source 5's incidents section was truncated in the provided text and could not be reviewed.

deployments.customer_or_partner: China Media Group (CCTV) Spring Festival Gala, directed by Zhang Yimou
deployments.site_or_context: CCTV Spring Festival Gala broadcast, China
deployments.task: Choreographed Yangge dance performance with 16 H1 robots in the piece 《秧Bot》.
caveats: A scripted stage performance, not productive work or a commercial task.
Execution mode (autonomy versus operator commands) is not disclosed by Unitree.
The 16-unit count comes from Unitree; the handkerchief throw-and-catch and LiDAR adaptation details come from second-hand reporting.

deployments.customer_or_partner: Stanford University (HumanPlus) and Carnegie Mellon University (H2O)
deployments.task: Imitation-learning research including clothes folding and typing (Stanford HumanPlus), and real-time whole-body teleoperation (CMU H2O).
caveats: Reported through a secondary blog citing arXiv papers; the papers and any institution statement were not reviewed here.
The research robots were modified (added wrists, hands and head cameras; about 60 kg and 33 DoF).
No operating hours, success rates or unit counts published in the reviewed source.

Unitree's product page lists Video V1.0 through V4.0 without descriptions.

demos.teleoperation_notes: No source states the execution mode for these clips.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Unitree publishes no payload for the H1; the 30 kg figure exists only in one directory and the distributor lists the H1 payload row as blank, with 7-21 kg given for the H1-2 arm.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Do not use payload as a comparative strength for the H1.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No Unitree runtime figure; directories give 1 hour and 2 hours, neither measured. Only the 864 Wh quickly replaceable pack is official.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Endurance should stay near the floor of the evidence scale.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Autonomy is claimed only for walking/running. No autonomous manipulation or task has been demonstrated, and teleoperation is a documented mainstream use of the platform.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Credit locomotion only; do not credit task autonomy.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Stock H1 ships without hands and with 4-DoF arms; manipulation evidence comes from labs that rebuilt the robot.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Manipulation dexterity should be scored on the platform's ceiling, not on HumanPlus/H2O results as shipped.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No named commercial customer, operating hours, throughput or intervention data found; use is research and stage performance.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Deployment proof stays well below tier 4.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Five YouTube sources were supplied with titles only and no transcripts, so no behaviour was characterised from them; the incident section of the RoboZaps review was truncated in the supplied text.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Demonstrated-behaviour claims rest on secondary descriptions; manual video review is required.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: The H1 is still listed but is quote-only, the H1-2 appears delisted, and Unitree's newer H2 is the promoted platform; no formal discontinuation notice exists.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Treat as a legacy-but-purchasable research platform.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: The H1 is a real, purchasable, human-sized biped whose public evidence is concentrated in locomotion and spectacle: a company-claimed 3.3 m/s record, four golds at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games, a contested 10.1 m/s peak from a modified unit, and a 16-robot televised dance. Manipulation, endurance, payload and commercial deployment evidence is thin or absent, most third-party numbers conflict, and the robot ships without hands.
strongest_positive_evidence: Public competition results: 1500 m gold in 6:34.40 and 400 m gold in 1:28.03 at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games, plus four golds per RobotsGuide.
Unitree's 3.3 m/s spec with >5 m/s potential and 360 N.m knee torque, on an 864 Wh swappable pack.
Sixteen H1s performed on a national broadcast (Unitree's own record).
Adopted as a research platform by Stanford (HumanPlus) and CMU (H2O), and documented with a full SDK, teleoperation and RL tooling.
Real purchasability with public price bands (about $90,000 anchor; EUR 93,496 excluding VAT from a distributor).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No Unitree payload, runtime or failure-rate disclosure; directories give 1 h versus 2 h and an uncorroborated 30 kg payload.
No autonomous manipulation or productive task demonstration; the stock robot has no hands and 4-DoF arms.
No named commercial customer, operating hours or output metric.
No independent benchmark, third-party measurement or safety certification.
No video verified in this review; all supplied YouTube sources lacked transcripts.
conflicting_claims: DoF: 18 per Unitree's per-limb counts versus 19 in the H1 URDF, RoboHub and RobotsGuide.
Speed: 3.3 m/s (Unitree spec, distributor table) versus 1500 mm/sec (Robot Report at launch, matching the distributor's 5.4 km/h description) versus 6 km/h (RobotsGuide).
Runtime: 1 hour (RobotsGuide) versus 2 hours (RoboHub); Unitree publishes none.
Payload: 30 kg (RoboHub only) versus no published figure and a blank H1 payload row at the distributor.
Price: 'below $90,000' expected in 2023 versus a $90,000 contact-us store anchor versus EUR 93,496 excluding VAT versus US $90,000-110,000 (RobotsGuide).
H1 versus H1-2 numbers (27 DoF, 70 kg, <2 m/s, 7-21 kg arm load) are frequently merged in secondary summaries.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit autonomous manipulation; the stock H1 has no hands and no manipulation demo exists.
Do not treat the 30 kg payload as a Unitree specification.
Do not describe the 3.3 m/s figure as Guinness-certified, and do not present 10.1 m/s as a sustained or stock-robot speed.
Do not transfer H1-2 specifications (27 DoF, 70 kg, 7-21 kg arm load, Dex5-1 hands) to the H1.
Do not credit HumanPlus or H2O manipulation results to the shipped robot; those robots were heavily modified.
Do not treat the Spring Festival Gala performance as proof of autonomous task execution.
Do not claim the H1 ran the Beijing half-marathon or the Hangzhou kickboxing bouts; those were G1s.
Do not assert discontinuation: no Unitree announcement exists.
researcher_notes.compilation_note: This pack was compiled automatically from the listed public sources on 2026-10-30 and needs human review before use in scoring. Verbatim excerpts, source dates and the H1/H1-2 split should be checked by a human, and the referenced videos and papers should be reviewed directly.

currentness.currentness_notes: The H1 is still listed on Unitree's site and store as of this review, but it is quote-only, the H1-2 appears delisted, and Unitree's H2 (from $29,900) is the platform it now promotes; the 2026 Spring Festival Gala featured G1s and the H2 rather than the H1. No formal discontinuation was found.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: The Unitree H1 is a full-size bipedal humanoid (about 180 cm, about 47 kg, 18 DoF by Unitree's per-limb counts, 864 Wh swappable battery) sold mainly to research labs through quote-based sales: Unitree's store shows a $90,000 'contact us' anchor and a European distributor lists it from EUR 93,496 excluding VAT. Its strongest public evidence is locomotion and spectacle, including a company-claimed 3.3 m/s record, 1500 m and 400 m golds at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games (6:34.40 and 1:28.03) and a second source crediting four track golds, a choreographed 16-robot national broadcast performance, and a company-claimed 10.1 m/s peak from a modified ~62 kg unit. Manipulation is weak: the stock robot ships without hands and with 4-DoF arms, and the manipulation literature (Stanford HumanPlus, CMU H2O) used heavily modified units. Unitree publishes no payload, runtime, failure-rate or deployment metrics; autonomy is asserted for walking and running only; third-party runtime figures conflict (1 h versus 2 h) and no independent benchmark or safety certification exists.
strongest_evidence: 1500 m gold in 6:34.40 and 400 m gold in 1:28.03 at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games, corroborated by a second source reporting four track golds (unitree-h1_evidence_005, unitree-h1_evidence_011).
Unitree's official spec page: about 180 cm, 47 kg, 3.3 m/s with >5 m/s potential, 18 DoF, 864 Wh replaceable battery, 360 N.m joints (unitree-h1_evidence_001).
Sixteen H1s performing on CCTV's 2025 Spring Festival Gala, recorded by Unitree itself (unitree-h1_evidence_013).
Detailed official developer documentation covering joint limits, i5/i7 and Orin compute, MID-360 LiDAR, D435 camera, SDK, teleoperation and RL tooling (unitree-h1_evidence_004).
Real purchasability with public price bands from a distributor and Unitree's store (unitree-h1_evidence_006, unitree-h1_evidence_012).
weakest_evidence: No Unitree payload or runtime disclosure; directory figures conflict and are uncorroborated.
No autonomous manipulation or productive task demonstration; no hands in the stock configuration.
No named commercial deployment, operating hours or throughput.
No independent measurement, benchmark or safety certification.
Demonstrated-behaviour claims rest on secondary descriptions; no video was reviewed directly.
known_do_not_credit: Autonomous manipulation or dexterity of the stock H1.
The 30 kg payload and 2 hour runtime as manufacturer specifications.
A Guinness-certified speed record, or 10.1 m/s as a sustained or stock-robot speed.
H1-2 specifications (27 DoF, 70 kg, 7-21 kg arm load, Dex5-1 hands) as H1 capabilities.
HumanPlus and H2O manipulation results as shipped-product ability.
The Spring Festival Gala dance as evidence of autonomous task execution.
G1 events (Beijing half-marathon, Hangzhou kickboxing) as H1 results.
Any claim that the H1 is discontinued, or that it is a commercial industrial deployment.
